subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
AN f32/f64 PROTOTYPE SPLIT BETWEEN A DEFINITION AND ITS CONSUMERS IS NOT A DEFECT LIST - THE DEFINITION IS NOT AUTHORITY OVER A CONSUMER'S DECLARATION, AND THE CONSUMER'S OWN TARGET BYTES ARE. Midway's PS2-derived sources carried PER-TU float-returning shim declarations that genuinely disagree with the function's own definition, and the GameCube retail bytes were compiled from those disagreeing declarations. The project already recorded one instance as an idiom comment (controls.c: 'PS2-shim float-returning decl' for atan2); this law generalises it and gives it a measurement procedure. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE EXTERNCHECK TABLE: the eleven same-arity f32/f64 prototype rows flagged as the highest-value queue by claim.externcheck-widened-defect-table-20260831.v1 are NOT eleven latent FindClosestWaypoint-class exacts. FindClosestWaypoint was exactable because its DEFINITION carried the wrong width and the definition's own frame floor was therefore wrong; all eleven of these definitions are ALREADY byte-exact, so no parameter-save-area floor is available to move and the param-floor law has no purchase on any of them. Check the defining function's match status FIRST - it is free and it settles the entire question.

THE THREE-WAY DISCRIMINATOR, applied per consumer TU, cheapest first. (1) IS THE CALLER ALREADY EXACT? If the function containing the call site measures real 0, its current declaration is correct-as-shipped and changing it is a pure regression - this is a VETO, and it costs one fuzzy.py read. newcam.c's 'extern double cos(double)' looks like an obvious outlier against seven sibling TUs that all declare 'f32 cos(f32)', yet DebugCamControlInputs is byte-exact with it: the outlier spelling IS the shipped one. (2) DOES THE TARGET LOAD THE ARGUMENT CONSTANT WITH lfs OR lfd? A float-literal argument is the channel that makes a parameter width VISIBLE: an f32 parameter materialises the literal with lfs, an f64 parameter with lfd. This is the positive-evidence case and it is decisive in both directions - it improved boss.c (nine lfd -> nine lfs, see below) and it refuted player.c (target lfs where our f64 declaration produced lfd). (3) DOES AN frsp APPEAR? A consumer that narrows the result to f32 emits frsp under an f64 return declaration and none under an f32 one, so a spurious or missing frsp names the return width directly.

DIRECTION MATTERS, AND IT IS THE PART A BATCH FIX GETS WRONG. Moving a LONE OUTLIER TU onto the image-majority spelling was byte-identical or better in every case measured (boss.c Random f64->f32 IMPROVED, sfx.c Random, items.c FloorPos, mb_blit.c __cvt_fp2unsigned, sndfx.c DistanceToClosestPlayer, bosscam.c NormalVector2D - all byte-identical). Moving the MAJORITY onto the definition's spelling was refuted every time it produced any evidence at all: mbBlitCvtCoord's definition takes f64 and eight consumer TUs declare f32, and player.c proves the f32 consumers are right. So majority-among-consumers, not the definition, is the prior - and where the bytes are silent, the existing declaration wins by default because there is no evidence to overturn it.

WHAT THIS DOES TO claim.law.parameter-save-area-width-sets-the-local-block-floor.20260901.v1. That law is unchanged where it applies (a wrong width in a function's OWN definition still sets its frame floor), but its scope is narrower than its text implies: it is a DEFINITION-side law only, and its central claim that 'an f32 and an f64 parameter are INDISTINGUISHABLE in the instruction stream' is false on the CONSUMER side, where a float-literal argument distinguishes them via lfs-versus-lfd. That is a second independent counter-example to the same sentence, joining the fmuls guard already recorded by attempt.bb-stringtextwidthsub-param-floor-refuted-pad-axis-closed.20260901.v1. Read the two together: the instruction stream is silent about float width only inside a function that neither spills the parameter nor is handed a literal for it.

RETAINED RESULT THAT ANCHORS THE POSITIVE HALF: boss.c declared 'extern f64 Random(f64)' against ml_fmath.c's exact 'f32 Random(f32)'. BossSpewCoins calls Random(0.1f) nine times; fndiff --ops read 'target-only: +9 lfs / ours-only: -9 lfd' with nine one-for-one replace rows. Correcting the declaration alone took BossSpewCoins real 139 -> 123, opcode-multiset tokens 31t -> 13t, fuzzy 90.23% -> 93.12%, with no sibling regression.
